title: 2010 HMMT February Algebra Problem 4
statement: Suppose that there exist nonzero complex numbers \(a, b, c\), and \(d\) such that \(k\) is a root of both the equations \(a x^{3}+b x^{2}+c x+d=0\) and \(b x^{3}+c x^{2}+d x+a=0\). Find all possible values of \(k\) (including complex values).

solutions.text: \(1,-1, i,-i\) Let \(k\) be a root of both polynomials. Multiplying the first polynomial by \(k\) and subtracting the second, we have \(a k^{4}-a=0\), which means that \(k\) is either \(1,-1, i\), or \(-i\). If \(a=b=c=d=1\), then \(-1, i\), and \(-i\) are roots of both polynomials. If \(a=b=c=1\) and \(d=-3\), then 1 is a root of both polynomials. So \(k\) can be \(1,-1, i\), and \(-i\).
